hits.text: 27 June — 2026 European heatwaves: The highest recorded temperature in Germany is taken in Möckern-Drewitz, measuring 41.5 °C (106.7 °F).
The 2026 European heatwaves begin, bringing record-breaking temperatures to several European countries and causing thousands of deaths over the next several weeks.

2026 United Kingdom heatwaves: A temperature of 35.1° C is recorded in Wisley, Surrey, which the Met Office reports is the eighth day above 34° C in 2026, a new UK record for the most number of 34° C or higher days in a calendar year.

26 May – During the late-May heat wave, France records its hottest May day in history, with the national thermal indicator reaching 24.8 °C (76.6 °F). Seven people die from causes linked directly or indirectly to the heat, while hundreds of weather stations set monthly temperature records and Météo-France activates its national heat-warning system in May for the first time since its introduction in 2004.

France experiences its hottest day on a national scale, with an average temperature of 29.8°C (85.6°F) across the country, beating the previous record of 29.4°C. The highest locally recorded temperature is 44.3°C, in Pissos.
